title: Classes and data objects
theory:
### Modeling records cleanly

Plain classes work, but **dataclasses** (`@dataclass`) generate `__init__`,
repr, comparisons, and more—perfect for simple aggregates. For lightweight,
immutable tuples with named fields, use `typing.NamedTuple`. When modeling dict
shapes with known keys, `typing.TypedDict` bridges structured dict literals and
static checking.

### Defaults and mutability

Dataclass field defaults follow the same rule as functions: never put mutable
defaults directly in the field list—use `field(default_factory=list)` instead.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Profile:
    handle: str
    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


p = Profile("neo")
p.tags.append("learners")
```

exercises.title: Define a Struct
exercises.description: Define a Person struct with Name (string) and Age (int). Create a Person with Name="Alice" and Age=30. Print it.
hints: __init__ stores attributes; customize __repr__ for brace output.

exercises.title: Pointer to Struct
exercises.description: Define a Point struct with X and Y (int). Create a pointer to Point{X: 5, Y: 10}. Use the pointer to change Y to 20. Print the Point.
hints: Instantiate Point(5, 10) assigning fields on self.
Mutate axis values before emitting brace-style coordinates.

exercises.title: Struct Literal
exercises.description: Given a Book struct with Title, Author, and Pages (int), create a Book instance using just Title and Author. Print it.
hints: __repr__ controls Book echo including spacing quirks when author empty.
Call Book(title=...) using the seeded title literal so braces match the checker.

exercises.title: Embedded Struct
exercises.description: Define Person with Name string, and Employee embedded Person with Company string. Create Employee with Name="Bob" and Company="Acme". Print Company.

exercises.title: Zero Value Struct
exercises.description: Declare a variable of type Rectangle with Width and Height (float) without initialization. Print it to see zero values.
hints: __repr__ emits ints converted from floats for widths/heights defaults.

exercises.title: Struct Comparison
exercises.description: Define a Config struct with Host (string) and Port (int). Create two Config values with identical fields and compare them using ==. Print the result.
hints: Lower-case textual booleans come from str(obj == obj).lower().

exercises.title: Modify Struct Field
exercises.description: Define a Counter struct with Value int (starts at 0). Create counter, increment Value by 5. Print the Value.
hints: Mutate counters with augmented assignment on instances.
exercises.solution:
class Counter:
    def __init__(self): self.value = 0

c = Counter()
c.value += 5
print(c.value)
